newsitem.title: USA: Colonial to shut gasoline line for 24-hour repairs.
newsitem.headline: Colonial to shut gasoline line for 24-hour repairs.

text.p: The Colonial Pipeline Co. will halt gasoline shipments for about 24 hours through its 1.2 million barrels per day (bpd) line for maintenance on January 16, according to a source at the company.
The one-day shutdown of Line One has been worked into the pipeline's schedule over a course of several weeks, the source said, and no delays to scheduled deliveries will occur.

The pipeline, the main artery between "refinery row" in Houston and the Northeast, will be taken out of service for work at the Amite River in Louisiana and further up the line in Mississippi, the source said.
The arterial Colonial Pipeline extends from Houston to Linden, New Jersey, on the edge of New York Harbor and includes a 960,000 bpd distillate line as well as the gasoline line.

Ten companies make up the Atlanta-based Colonial consortium including Amoco Corp, Atlantic Richfield Co, Petroleos de Venezuela SA's Citgo Petroleum Co unit, DuPont Co's Conoco Inc, Mobil Corp, Phillips Petroleum Co, Texaco Inc, Union Oil, a unit of Unocal Corp, and Marathon Oil Co, a unit of USX-Marathon Group.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1626
